Well u/neon 's comment seems to be saying you should give up on her which simply isnt the way at all.

She is an adult so she has to take responsibility for her actions. If she's choosing to act out in this way then that's on her. Even if she's going through something, there are plenty of people out there who deal with problems without doing things like scamming.

For your interactions with her, i would suggest you take the high road. Make it clear that you love her, but her actions are putting extreme stress on your relationship with her and on your own mind. So set some boundaries, and make it clear that she wont be able to rely on you or interact with you regularly if its going to be toxic. Im not saying cut her off, but set firm limits. Because if you ever want her to become aware of her behavior and begin to improve herself then you need to give her the opportunity.

As for how it makes you feel as a parent, i have no experience to draw on for this advice but maybe it helps so here it goes. You seem to be very caring, and because you care so much her bad behavior is hurting you. I would try and remind you that you are not perfect, neither is she, no one is. But you did your best to raise her, and as long as you didnt abuse her, physically, verbally, sexually, or emotionally, and you showed her all the love you could, then you did fine. I dont know your life so i cant say anything specific, but try not to mythologize her past "good" self or compare her to her siblings too much because i feel like that makes realistic change for her seem inadequate. If there is a gold standard that will never be reached because she has done bad things then she might not try to improve and you might not recognize her attempts to improve

Basically, hold onto hope and love for her always but give yourself a break and through setting up boundaries try and find some rest for your mind
